title: Greibach normal form for conjunctive grammars
formal: Does every conjunctive language \(L\subseteq\Sigma^*\) with \(\varepsilon\notin L\) have an equivalent conjunctive grammar all of whose rules are of the form \[A\to a\beta_1\mathbin{\&}\cdots\mathbin{\&}a\beta_k,\qquad a\in\Sigma,\quad k\ge1,\quad\beta_i\in N^*\,?\]
definitions: A conjunctive grammar has a finite terminal alphabet Sigma, a disjoint finite set N of nonterminals, a start symbol S, and finitely many rules A→alpha_1 & … & alpha_k, with k≥1 and alpha_i∈(Sigma∪N)*. Interpret a terminal as its singleton language, a word of symbols as concatenation of their languages, a conjunction as intersection, and alternative rules for A as union. The language tuple is the least fixed point of these monotone equations, equivalently the union of their iterations starting with empty nonterminal languages. An empty right-hand-side word denotes {epsilon}; a nonterminal with no rules denotes the empty language. No negation appears in the grammar. In the required normal form all conjuncts of any one rule begin with the same terminal a, followed only by nonterminals. The strings beta_i may be empty, so A→a is permitted. There is no upper bound on the number of conjuncts or length of beta_i other than finiteness of the grammar. Different rules may start with different terminals. No epsilon production or nonterminal-only unit rule is allowed in the output. The empty language is included and is represented by a start nonterminal with no rules. New nonterminals are allowed, but the terminal alphabet and the generated language must be exactly preserved. This is an existence-of-normal-form question; it does not additionally require a polynomial-size or effective translation.
answer_criterion: Prove the normal-form existence theorem in Lean for every epsilon-free conjunctive language, or supply a conjunctive language without epsilon and prove that no grammar of the displayed form generates it. A theorem whose hypotheses already assume Greibach normal form does not establish its general existence.
context:
Kuznetsov represents languages of conjunctive grammars already in Greibach normal form in an enriched Lambek calculus. That hypothesis is central to the scope of the result.

Okhotin’s hardest-language construction explicitly notes that equality of the Greibach-form class with all conjunctive languages is not known in that work.
why: A Greibach form would impose input-consuming recursion on a broad extension of context-free grammar.

import_provenance.original_title: A Greibach normal form for conjunctive grammars
import_provenance.original_statement: Can every conjunctive language not containing the empty word be generated with rules A→aβ₁ & ⋯ & aβₖ, where each βᵢ is a string of nonterminals? Such a normal form would ensure that each recursive expansion consumes an input symbol, generalizing a fundamental theorem for context-free grammars.
